clue.text: Cheek, and what is at the bottom of it

definitions.meaning: cheek in the sense of impudence or brass nerve

definitions.text: what is at the bottom of it
definitions.meaning: the part of the body below the face, joining the head to the shoulders

explanation.surface: A question about anatomy: the cheek, and whatever lies beneath it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' seems to point back to the cheek as a part of the face; read the first word as cheeky nerve instead, and the second definition is the part of the body underneath the head.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: brazen impudence is a common British slang meaning, and the body part sits directly beneath the face.

clue.text: Young girl in city on speed

indicators.note: on, in a down clue, puts the city above the speed units

parts.note: NY is the abbreviation for New York City
mph is miles per hour, a measure of speed

explanation.surface: A young girl in a city is on drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'speed' suggests amphetamines, but it means the unit of speed. 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: In mythology a nymph is a beautiful young female spirit, and poetically any young maiden.

clue.text: Turn up with a ring, on top of the world

parts.note: to cock is to turn up, as in cocking a hat brim or an ear
a hoop is a circular band or ring

explanation.surface: Someone appears with an engagement ring, feeling elated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn up' looks like 'arrive', but it means to tilt upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer means exultant and boastfully delighted, an idiom for feeling elated.

clue.text: Investigator robbed of ecstasy in drug scandal, perhaps

indicators.note: in says the trimmed investigator is placed inside the drug's letters

parts.note: opium is a narcotic drug made from poppies

indicators.note: robbed of says a letter is stolen away from the investigator word

parts.note: a prober is someone who investigates
E is the usual abbreviation for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A detective loses his ecstasy pills in a drugs scandal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'robbed of' strips the ecstasy from the investigator, and 'in' sets what is left into the drug. 'perhaps' marks the definition as an example: a scandal brings public disgrace.
explanation.definitionFit: Opprobrium is public disgrace or harsh condemnation, the kind of shame a scandal brings on someone.

clue.text: Mate in airport — bob, perhaps

parts.note: a pal is a friend or mate
taken as written
drome is short for aerodrome, an airfield or airport

explanation.surface: A friend in an airport is called Bob.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bob' is the example: the word bob reads the same backwards. In the surface it looks like a name (the capital is hidden at its start).
explanation.definitionFit: The word bob reads the same in both directions, so it is an example of a word symmetrical in spelling.

clue.text: Sounds like a capital ramble

indicators.note: sounds like says the word is heard, spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: Rome is the capital of Italy

explanation.surface: Wandering a capital city sounds like a nice idea.
explanation.definitionFit: To wander without a fixed route is a synonym for rambling.

clue.text: Cover county, about to walk round it

parts.note: Beds is the abbreviation of Bedfordshire, an English county

indicators.note: round it says the walking word goes around the about word

parts.note: to pad is to walk softly
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Covering a county's territory, ready to walk round it.
explanation.walkthrough: Bedfordshire is a county north of London. 'round it' has the walking word wrap around 'about', the 'it' of the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A decorative top layer over a bed is the bed's cover.

clue.text: I tucked into dessert, beginning to relish what's colder

indicators.note: tucked into says the letter I goes inside the dessert

parts.note: an ice is a frozen dessert

indicators.note: beginning to takes only the first letter of the word relish

explanation.surface: Someone eats a dessert with relish because it's chilled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tucked into' suggests eating but here places I inside ICE to give ICIE.
explanation.definitionFit: More frozen means having a lower temperature, so the comparative synonym fits.

clue.text: Can fellow sink emigrants' vessel?

parts.note: may means can, being permitted to
to lower is to sink or let down

explanation.surface: A question whether a man might sink a ship of emigrants.
explanation.walkthrough: The Mayflower carried the Pilgrim Fathers from England to America in 1620.
explanation.definitionFit: The ship took English Puritan settlers across the Atlantic to found Plymouth Colony.

clue.text: Old guard has to pull up

indicators.note: up, in a down clue, says the pulling word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: to draw is to pull

explanation.surface: A veteran sentry has to stop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pull up' looks like stopping, but 'up' turns DRAW. 'Old' marks the archaic sense, as in 'watch and ward'.
explanation.definitionFit: In older English the word meant keeping watch or protection, a guard.

clue.text: Bloomer by archangel? Dismay as disorder follows

indicators.note: follows puts the rearranged letters after the archangel's name

parts.note: Michael is one of the archangels named in the Bible

indicators.note: disorder says the letters of the words dismay as are thrown into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone makes a blunder worthy of an archangel, and dismay spreads.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomer' looks like a blunder but means a flower. 'disorder' rearranges 'Dismay as', and 'follows' puts the result after the archangel.
explanation.definitionFit: A Michaelmas daisy is an autumn-flowering aster, so it is literally a plant that blooms.

clue.text: Collecting a screen of boards

definitions.meaning: a temporary fence of planks, often used for posters, around a building site

explanation.surface: Someone gathering a fence made of wooden panels.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: stockpiling goods, and a British word for a billboard or a site fence of planks.

clue.text: Corkscrew? It's not needed for shorts and beer, mostly

indicators.note: not needed for says the words it's are taken away from the drinks word that follows

parts.note: shorts are small drinks of spirits, as opposed to long drinks
it's, spelt without its apostrophe, gives three letters

indicators.note: mostly says the beer word loses its final letter

parts.note: ale is a type of beer

explanation.surface: A drinker ponders whether a corkscrew is needed for whisky chasers and pints.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not needed for' takes ITS out of SPIRITS, leaving SPIR; 'mostly' cuts ALE to AL. In British pubs a short is a small measure of spirits. The question mark marks the definition: a corkscrew's shape is an example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A coil winding round and round is a corkscrew shape, so the question mark signals an example of the shape.

clue.text: Effect of dripping in prison on small child

indicators.note: on, in a down clue, puts the prison above the child

parts.note: a stalag was a German prisoner-of-war camp
a mite is a small child

explanation.surface: Water drips into a prison onto a small child.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link word between definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Limestone deposits built up by water falling from a cave roof form this rising column.

clue.text: They're instrumental in depriving tramps of aspiration

indicators.note: depriving says a letter is taken away from the word for tramps

parts.note: a hobo is an American word for a tramp, here plural
aspiration is the breathy sound written as the letter H

explanation.surface: Something is helping to stop vagrants from having ambitions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'instrumental' reads as 'helpful' but points to musical instruments. 'aspiration' is not ambition: in phonetics it is the breathed H sound, which 'depriving' drops.
explanation.definitionFit: Woodwind instruments with double reeds are, quite literally, instrumental things.

clue.text: Government official's given order to take us pals over castle, perhaps

indicators.note: over, in a down clue, puts the pals above the castle

parts.note: OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour
bud is American slang for a pal or friend
in chess a castle, or rook, is an example of a man, or piece

explanation.surface: An official is ordered to escort American friends over a castle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'us' is not the pronoun but US, so 'US pals' means American friends. The Order of Merit is a British award.
explanation.definitionFit: This public official investigates complaints against government bodies on behalf of citizens.

clue.text: Uniform result of milliner's handiwork

parts.note: a milliner makes headwear, and one item made could belong to the outfit of a naval rating

explanation.definitionFit: A milliner makes headgear, and this is the round brimmed cap worn with a naval rating's uniform.

clue.text: Where to see riders making a dreadful din

parts.note: rotten means very bad or dreadful
a row is a loud noise or racket

explanation.surface: A loud, unpleasant noise is heard from somewhere riders can be seen.
explanation.walkthrough: Rotten Row is a track for horse riding along the south side of Hyde Park in London.
explanation.definitionFit: The London bridle path is a famous place for horse riders to exercise their mounts.

clue.text: Car racket could be made out here

indicators.note: could be made out says the letters of car racket can be remade into something new

explanation.surface: Engine noise from a car can be heard here.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the single word 'here': the clue reads as an &lit-style picture of a noisy motor-racing venue.
explanation.definitionFit: A noisy car would be heard at a motor circuit, the place the clue's 'here' points to.

clue.text: Lamp's a bit dodgy during church service

indicators.note: dodgy means unreliable or faulty, telling us the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A church lamp is faulty during the service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dodgy' rearranges the letters of LAMPS A BIT. The definition is an adjectival phrase: the answer describes what happens at a christening.
explanation.definitionFit: Baptism is a church rite of initiation, so anything happening at it is described by this adjective.

clue.text: Firm investing in the German scenery

indicators.note: investing in suggests the firm being placed inside the article

parts.note: der is a German word for the
Co. is the abbreviation for company, a firm

explanation.surface: A company puts money into the German stage sets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'investing' looks financial but here means going inside: the firm sits within the German article.
explanation.definitionFit: Decor is the furnishing and decoration of a place, including a stage set's scenery.

clue.text: One of the borrowers, a girl who's come out to run

parts.note: a deb, or debutante, is a young woman who has made her formal entry into society
taken as written
R is the cricket abbreviation for a run

explanation.surface: A debutante is about to dash off, as one of a group of borrowers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'come out' is not an anagram signal: it refers to a debutante's coming out into high society.
explanation.definitionFit: Anyone who borrows money owes it, and so is in the class of people who owe.

clue.text: Lord with nothing in store

indicators.note: in says the zero goes inside the store word

parts.note: a barn is a farm building used as a store
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A nobleman has nothing in his storehouse.
explanation.definitionFit: A noble of the lowest rank in the British peerage is a lord.

clue.text: He doesn't believe in aimless coasting

indicators.note: aimless suggests the letters of coasting are wandering without direction

explanation.surface: A sceptic rejects the idea of drifting along without purpose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'aimless' rearranges COASTING. The definition stops at 'believe'; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who holds that the existence of God cannot be known does not commit to belief.

clue.text: Sign on, receiving a note

indicators.note: receiving says the word on holds the note within it

parts.note: me (mi) is the third note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Sign on, taking a note, perhaps for benefits.
explanation.walkthrough: To sign on in Britain is to register for unemployment benefit, which is the surface picture.
explanation.definitionFit: A portent or omen is a sign of things to come.

clue.text: Younger member of family Edward and bill brought up

indicators.note: brought up, in a down clue, says the joined pieces read upwards

parts.note: Ted is a short form of Edward
AC is the abbreviation for account, a bill

explanation.surface: Edward and a bill brought up for a family's youngest member.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought up' looks like raising children, but reverses TEDAC.
explanation.definitionFit: A younger son of a family, especially of a noble house, is traditionally called this.

clue.text: Employer some of you serve

indicators.note: some of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An employer is served by some of you.
explanation.walkthrough: The employer is not a boss: it is one who employs, or uses, something.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who employs a tool or service makes use of it.

clue.text: Island that may produce Washington's wife's wine

parts.note: Martha Washington was the wife of George Washington, the first US president
a vineyard is a plantation of grapevines: it is what may produce wine

explanation.surface: An island makes wine for the first US president's wife.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that may produce' links the two halves: a grape plantation is where wine comes from. The island is off Massachusetts.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer names an island off Cape Cod in Massachusetts, a summer resort.

clue.text: One of those not in the race, or entrants running

definitions.text: One of those not in the race

indicators.note: running suggests the letters of or entrants are moving about into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Describing horses absent from a race, or competitors taking part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'running' fits the racing surface but rearranges OR ENTRANTS.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse that is withdrawn before a race does not start, so it is absent from the field.

clue.text: Sketch of king in pose

indicators.note: in says the king's letter goes inside the word for pose

parts.note: to sit for a portrait is to pose
K is the abbreviation for king in chess and cards

explanation.surface: An artist draws a king who is posing for him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sketch' suggests drawing in this artistic scene, but it means a short comic performance.
explanation.definitionFit: A short comic piece in a revue is a sketch.
